extracted.intended_audience: lawyers, government officials, transparency advocates, and members of the public seeking summary of the Government in the Sunshine Act
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of statutory definitions, the openness requirement, procedural obligations, and the ten statutory exemptions under the U.S. Government in the Sunshine Act (5 U.S.C. §552b) that determine when agency meetings must be open to public observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'meeting'
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute defines a 'meeting' as 'the deliberations of at least the number of individual agency members required to take action on behalf of the agency where such deliberations determine or result in the joint conduct or disposition of official agency business.' 5 U.S.C. 552b(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A gathering counts as a meeting only if it involves deliberations by at least the number of members required to take agency action and those deliberations determine or result in joint official agency business; the openness requirement is only triggered when this definition is met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'agency'
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute defines 'agency' to include 'any agency ... headed by a collegial body composed of two or more individual members ... and any subdivision thereof authorized to act on behalf of the agency.' 5 U.S.C. 552b(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Act applies to entities that meet this definition (collegial bodies of two or more members and their authorized subdivisions); if the body is not an 'agency' as defined, the Act's requirements do not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness requirement (every portion open to public observation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sunshine Act provides, with ten specified exemptions, that 'every portion of every meeting of an agency shall be open to public observation.' 5 U.S.C. 552b(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a general rule agency meetings must be open to public observation. Closure is only allowed under one of the statutory exemptions and only after applicable procedural steps are followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notice and procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act 'imposes procedural requirements to ensure, inter alia, that advance notice is given to the public before agency meetings take place' and requires agencies to follow procedural requirements before determining that an exemption applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must provide public advance notice of meetings and must comply with prescribed procedures (e.g., making determinations and invoking statutory exemptions) before excluding the public; failure to follow procedures can defeat a claimed exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 1: information relating to national defense
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category permits closure of meeting portions when disclosure would divulge national defense information; must be assessed against statutory language and relevant classified-information rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 2: internal personnel rules and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Information related solely to internal personnel rules and practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matters that concern only internal agency personnel policies/practices (and not matters of public agency business) may be exempt from public observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 3: matters specifically protected by law
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If another statute specifically protects certain information from disclosure, that legal protection can justify closing a meeting or portion of it under this exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 4: trade secrets or privileged/confidential commercial information
rubrics_metrics.description: Trade secrets or privileged/confidential commercial information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may withhold portions of meetings that would reveal trade secrets or confidential commercial information to protect proprietary interests; applicability depends on confidentiality and privilege considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 5: matters censuring or accusing a person of a crime
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters censuring or accusing a person of a crime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussions that would censure or accuse individuals of criminal conduct may be closed to avoid prejudicial public disclosure and protect legal rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 6: information where disclosure would constitute a breach of privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Information where disclosure would constitute a breach of privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal privacy interests can justify closing portions of meetings where disclosure would intrude on individual privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 7: investigatory records harmful to proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Related to investigatory records where the information would harm the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disclosure of investigatory materials would harm ongoing investigations or related proceedings, those portions can be exempted from public observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 8: information for use by agencies regulating financial institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Information for the use of an agency responsible for the regulation or supervision of financial institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material prepared for or used by financial regulators in their supervisory or regulatory functions can be exempt to protect supervisory processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 9: information that would lead to financial speculation or endanger financial stability
rubrics_metrics.description: Information which would lead to financial speculation or endanger the stability of any financial institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure that could cause market speculation or threaten a financial institution's stability may be withheld to prevent economic harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 10: matters related to the agency's participation in legal proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Related to the agency's participation in legal proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussions concerning litigation strategy, privileged legal communications, or other aspects of agency participation in legal proceedings can justify closure under this exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triggering rule: requirements only apply when entity is an 'agency' and gathering is a 'meeting'
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the openness requirement nor the procedural requirements are triggered unless the governmental entity at issue is an 'agency,' and unless the gathering in question is a 'meeting' of the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before applying the Act's openness and exemption rules, determine (1) whether the body qualifies as an 'agency' under 5 U.S.C. 552b(a)(1) and (2) whether the gathering meets the statutory 'meeting' definition; if either element is absent, the Act's obligations do not apply.
